I was watching a YouTube video, sponsored by Audible, telling of Audible's offer to of a free download of your first audio book.

Sweet! I have a book I've been wanting to read, let me head over to this site and check it out.

Signed up (through Amazon), got my book, checked out, downloaded book. Cool, awesome, great service.

Having experience with automatic subscription renewal through amazon (Amazon Prime student), I thought now would be a good time to cancel the subscription before they charge me for another month, that I don't want, before i forget. Here is when the adventure begins....

I have canceled accounts before, we all have, so I was prepared for this process to be involved and a bit tricky, but not downright deceitful. To be fair, this process started out relatively easily compared to other sites, but *do not be fooled* by this false sense of accommodation. I head to my account page, and one of the three main options available is "Cancel Subscription."

Fantastic! Wow, they made this easy to find!

But wait, there's more...

I click the button, and there's no more friendly buttons, just plain text and hyperlinks. That's fine, like I said, this is something we've all done before. It's understandable. I search through the text and find the "manage my subscription" hyperlink and click on away to the next page.

Alright, not to bad. This is a lot easier than I thought this would be.

But wait, there's more!

The next page loads, and a great, friendly reminder of all the great features audible has to offer, accompanied by images and buttons that presumably take you to other portions of the site and away from this cancellation process. Scroll to the bottom and you'll find a drop down box asking you to select the reason why you're canceling the subscription. Next to that box is a nice, appealing red button reading, "I want all these awesome features" or some other bullshit and another one, white and less appealing, reading, "Cancel Subscription". Again, for a cancellation procedure, a fairly standard process, and something I was prepared for.

Wow, that was easy. Let's click continue, and then we're good to go!

But wait, there's more..?

This is where things become a bit absurd. Another page loads, containing mostly the same content as the previous page, only without the drop down box and using different graphics/organization. Confused as to whether or not my cancellation had gone through, I scrolled to the bottom of the page and hit the *exact same* "Cancel Subscription" button hoping that's it, *AND THE EXACT SAME PAGE RELOADS*. This repeats *one or two more times* until I'm finally redirected to a different page, this one nearly identical to the page with the drop down box except this time mostly in plaintext and hyperlinks. At this point, I'm more baffled than annoyed. I mean, what a blatant and shallow attempt to milk unwanting users of there hard-earned cash behind their backs. I'd go as far as to say I was a little *disgusted*, but I digress, and I click on to the final "Cancellation Confirmed" page.

Alas, the saga has finally completed. I write you from a far away land, as the journey to unsubscribe from Audible is long and trying. Needless to say, it is a trek not for the meek nor feeble. I write this letter more as a Public Service Announcement of sorts than a rant: **KEEP CLICKING THE "CANCEL SUBSCRIPTION" BUTTON UNTIL THERE IS NO MORE BUTTONS TO CLICK**. I hope that one day, this letter reaches a friend who hears of my woes, and bravely embarks on the journey to unsubscribe from their audible account in a bleak attempt to rescue me from this God forsaken land.

Sincerely,
